pointers.concern: Environment variable OSRS_TRACKER_DEV + OSRS_TRACKER_API_URL allows arbitrary override of the API base URL at runtime, redirecting all event uploads (including the Bearer apiToken in Authorization header) to any host. Anyone who can set env vars on the user's machine (or a malicious launcher script) can silently exfiltrate tokens, screenshots, and bank/video data.
pointers.why: getEffectiveApiUrl() is called by ApiClient and BingoProgressReporter with no allowlist or scheme check; combined with the Authorization: Bearer header this is a credential-leak primitive triggered purely via env config.

pointers.concern: Manifest description does not match implementation. Manifest lists only level-ups, quests, loot, clue scrolls, collection log, deaths + video. Code adds Item Snitch (scans and reports private bank contents to server), Bingo subscription/progress reporter (server-driven event subscription that pulls config and decides what to report+capture), Pet tracker, and a Quick Capture sidebar that uploads on-demand video. These are material new data-collection surfaces not disclosed in the plugin-hub description or tags.
pointers.why: Plugin-hub policy requires the description to accurately convey what data is sent and what features exist; bank scanning and server-driven capture rules are sensitive enough that users must be informed.

pointers.concern: Server-driven capture: BingoSubscriptionManager pulls a remote subscription that decides which NPC kills, items, loot values, raids, gauntlets, slayer tasks, and clues trigger an automatic video/screenshot upload (needsProofForNpcKill / needsProofForBossKill etc.). The remote backend can dynamically widen what events trigger media capture without any client-side allowlist or user prompt.
pointers.why: Effectively a remote-controlled recorder. Plugin-hub typically requires media capture to be user-initiated or clearly described; manifest does not mention bingo or remote-controlled proof capture.

pointers.concern: Item Snitch feature scans the player's bank contents and (per CLAUDE.md and config defaults itemSnitchReportSightings=true, trackItemSnitch=true) reports who has which 'shared items' to the API by default. Bank contents are sensitive personal account data; defaulting reporting to enabled without explicit user consent is a privacy concern, especially since the manifest does not mention bank scanning or item-sighting reporting.
pointers.why: Defaults send bank inventory data on first install; users following the manifest description would not expect bank-scan uploads.

pointers.concern: Quick Capture button captures up to ~10s of video plus a screenshot and POSTs it (with the local player's RSN) to /api/webhooks/quick_capture. Endpoint not mentioned in manifest; combined with VideoRecorder always running (startUp line 210) means a buffer of recent gameplay frames is continuously held in memory ready to upload.
pointers.why: Continuous frame buffering plus on-demand upload of recent game footage is a feature class users should be told about; manifest tags omit quick capture.

pointers.concern: 16 additional .java files in the diff are not shown, and several core files (DeathTracker, LootTracker, PetTracker, QuestTracker, SkillLevelTracker, VideoRecorder, AsyncFrameCapture, SoftwareFrameCapture) are listed as 'omitted to stay under token budget'. These include the video pipeline (which handles raw frame buffers and any native interop) and tracker classes that build outbound payloads. Cannot complete a security review of reflection / native loads / Runtime.exec / data fields without these files.
pointers.why: Hidden code in security-sensitive subsystems (video encoding, payload construction) prevents verification of the rest of this review's findings.

pointers.concern: Payload is built with `gson.fromJson(jsonPayload, JsonObject.class)` and then has base64 screenshot/video fields injected before re-serialization. If any caller passes user-controlled or untrusted text into jsonPayload (e.g. quest names, item names, RSN, chat-derived strings) a malformed JSON will throw and be caught silently (logged 'Failed to add screenshot/video') and the original raw string is sent. Not a classic vuln but error-handling masks payload corruption that could let injection attempts slip past silently.
pointers.why: Worth flagging because chat-message-derived strings (CollectionLogTracker uses regex on chat) flow into payloads; defensive escaping is implicit in Gson but the silent fallback weakens it.
